cells.tense: Present — you're here, and the shears are in your hand.
cells.verb: tending what's still growing while cutting back what's done
cells.place: in the middle of something ending that has to end for the next thing to have room
cells.ask: Let one person see what you're clearing away, and name it to them as finished rather than lost. What comes back when this is in balance: letting go stops feeling like losing and starts feeling like the work being complete.
cells.core:
You're clearing with care. Something is ending and you haven't rushed it and you haven't let it rot — you're taking out what's finished and keeping your hand on what's still alive, both at once, without one crowding out the other. That's the hard version of an ending, done well.

It doesn't have to stay private. Someone could see what you're setting down and know it cost you something.
cells.sheetLine: You're ending it carefully, and keeping what's still alive while you do.

cells.tense: Future — you're already living in the version where nothing gets lost.
cells.verb: managing every loose end of what's ending so none of it slips
cells.place: at a clearing that hasn't finished happening yet
cells.ask: Before you tidy one more thing, sit with what this already gave you and let it be enough as it stands. What comes back when this is in balance: the care stops exhausting you, and you can hold what's going without clutching it.
cells.core:
You're tending the ending ahead of itself. Somewhere down the line there's a version of this that closes clean — nothing wasted, nothing left in the wrong hands — and you're working toward it so hard that the thing can't actually finish. Every detail gets held, sorted, kept safe, and the holding has become the point.

The care is real. It's just arrived before there's anything to care for yet.
cells.sheetLine: You're so busy managing how it ends that it can't.

cells.tense: Past — the ending is behind you, and you're still standing where it was.
cells.verb: not tending what's left, so the finished and the living sit together untouched
cells.place: at a door that's already closed
cells.ask: Don't go back and sort the wreckage. Instead, find the one thing you still actually hope for and put your hands on that — tend it a little, this week. What comes back when this is in balance: the clearing starts happening on its own, and the care stops feeling like effort.
cells.core:
The ending came and the tending stopped. Something is finished, and what's still alive from it and what's dead from it are standing in the same ground, because nobody's gone in to tell them apart. It isn't that you don't care. It's that caring here feels like it means going back, and you haven't.

The way through isn't back. It's forward, toward whatever you still want.
cells.sheetLine: It's over, and you haven't gone in to clear it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — you're writing this ending and calling it weather.
cells.verb: already deciding what stays and what goes, quietly, by hand
cells.place: in a clearing you keep describing as something that just happened
cells.ask: Say it plainly to one person: I chose to let this end. What comes back when this is in balance: the letting-go reads as yours, and what you kept stops needing an excuse.
cells.core:
You're already doing the clearing. What gets kept, what gets let go, what gets a little more time — you're making those calls, carefully, and the shape of things shows it. But when you talk about it, it's circumstance. Things ran their course. It was just time.

The tending is yours. The ending is yours too. The only thing missing is you saying so.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing what ends. You keep saying it just did.
